posts.title: Player Ratings: USMNT cruise past Haiti in Poch's farewell
posts.description: Ok, I’m going to go out with gratitude. Ready? Mauricio Pochettino, who managed his last match for the US men’s national team tonight, did a number of good things for the program. For one, he brought name recognition to the job simply by being Mauricio Pochettino, a globally recognized manager with a resume that nobody in the program's history could really match. You could quibble about how important that actually is; I’m willing to hear either side of it. But I think where I’ve come down is that, for a program desperate to grow but lacking credibility in the eyes of the casuals that comprise the vast majority of the US fanbase, it mattered quite a bit. For two, he implemented an attractive, aggressive style of play, and, credit where it's due, did so by building upon the foundation Gregg Berhalter had laid rather than coming in and lighting the whole thing on fire.
